content: Morley is a fictional brand of cigarettes, seemingly inspired by the shortened name for Marlboro cigarettes, Marleys. This brand has been featured in various television shows and movies, often as a subtle nod or plot device. In the movie 200 Cigarettes, Lucy (played by Courtney Love) gives a block of Morley cigarettes to Kevin (played by Paul Rudd). The title of the film refers to the number of cigarettes in a carton (20 cigarettes per pack, 10 packs per carton). In the online cartoon Broken Saints, the character Raimi purchases a pack of Morley cigarettes. Interestingly, William B. Davis, known for his role in The X-Files, is part of the voice cast. However, the creator of Broken Saints, Brooke Burgess, clarified that Morley cigarettes were included in the series long before Davis joined the project, though Davis appreciated the reference. In Buffy the Vampire Slayer, Spike (played by James Marsters) is seen smoking Morley cigarettes. There was a misquote by Zap2it, where Marsters was reported to have said, We smoke Morleys. We both smoke the same brand. We’re the only two characters on TV that do, referring to himself and William B. Davis from The X-Files. In the Cold Case episode The Plan, Jerry smokes Morleys. During an interrogation scene, Detective Nick Vera removes a cigarette from Jerry's hand after it burns down to his fingers. In the Criminal Minds episode North Mammon, a pile of Morley cigarette butts leads the FBI team to suspect a soccer coach of stalking one of his star female players. DNA analysis of the cigarette butts implicates the coach. However, upon closer inspection of the footage, the cigarette pack he holds is actually a Marlboro pack, not a Morley pack. In the ER episode Beyond Repair, Morley cigarettes make an appearance. In the movie Freddy Got Fingered, Gord (played by Tom Green) is seen smoking a pack of Morleys in one scene. In the film Gun Shy, during a meeting between the police, the character Charley has a box of Morley cigarettes in front of him on the conference table. In the 1970 TV movie House on Greenapple Road, a character steals a pack of Morley cigarettes from a desk at the police station. In the movie 0, a terrorist disguises powerful explosives as a pack of Morley cigarettes and demonstrates their destructive power by detonating a piece of swamp in the Philippines. In the Killer Instinct episode Game Over, Lt. Matt Cavanaugh (played by Chi McBride) is seen with Morley cigarettes on his desk. In an episode of Malcolm in the Middle, a pack of Morley cigarettes is one of the items hidden by Malcolm's mother. In the Millennium episode The Time Is Now, Peter Watts discovers a Morley cigarette stub in the mysterious Millennium Group's basement. This is a nod to the Cigarette Smoking Man from The X-Files, as both series were created by Chris Carter. In the original Mission Impossible television series, Morley cigarettes appear, with several characters seen holding them. In the Nash Bridges episode Power Play, Morley cigarettes are visible on a desk in a criminal's house. In Prison Break season 2, episode 11, T-Bag picks up a pack of Morleys from a bag in Roy's apartment. In an episode of The Outer Limits, a man boarding a bus is seen with a pack of Morley cigarettes. In the movie Prozac Nation, the character played by Christina Ricci smokes Morley cigarettes. Ricci's character, a young writer, occasionally uses the empty cigarette packs as scrap paper. In the Space: Above and Beyond episode Ray Butts, the main character, Ray Butts, has a pack of Morleys at the beginning of the episode. In the Special Unit 2 episode The Grain, a housewife under the influence of the Sandman robs a convenience store, demanding all the cash and a pack of Morleys. In the movie Spy Game, Morley cigarettes are featured. In the That '70s Show episode Eric Gets Suspended, Red Forman tells Eric Forman to smoke an entire pack of Morleys after Eric is caught with a cigarette at school. In the Thirteen movie, Morley cigarettes are seen. In the Twilight Zone episode Nightmare at 20,000 Feet (September 1963), William Shatner's character pulls out a pack of Morleys and almost lights one until his wife (played by Christine White) points out the illuminated NO SMOKING sign on the plane. This is the earliest known reference to Morley cigarettes. In The X-Files, the Cigarette Smoking Man (played by William B. Davis) smokes Morley cigarettes. This is perhaps the most iconic use of the fictional brand. In one episode, Mulder and Scully even visit Morley's headquarters after one of their employees is murdered.
